content: The Online Computer Library Center, Inc. (OCLC) is a nonprofit organization that provides computer-based library services and conducts research to enhance access to global information while reducing associated costs. It was established in 1967 as the Ohio College Library Center. Currently, over 60,000 libraries in 112 countries and territories utilize OCLC services for locating, acquiring, cataloging, lending, and preserving library materials. The organization was founded by Fred Kilgour and is headquartered in Dublin, Ohio, USA. In 2002, OCLC acquired NetLibrary, the largest provider of electronic content. OCLC also owns 100% of the shares of OCLC PICA, a library automation systems and services company based in Leiden, Netherlands, which was renamed OCLC in late 2007. In June 2006, the Research Libraries Group (RLG) merged into OCLC. On January 11, 2008, OCLC announced its acquisition of EZproxy. OCLC offers bibliographic, abstract, and full-text information to libraries, students, faculty, scholars, and other information seekers. Together with its member libraries, OCLC collaboratively produces and maintains WorldCat, the largest online public access catalog (OPAC) in the world. WorldCat contains holding records from most public and private libraries globally and is accessible through many libraries and university computer networks. The Open WorldCat program makes records of library-owned materials in the WorldCat database available to web users via popular internet search engines, bibliographic platforms, and bookselling websites. This initiative enhances the accessibility of member libraries' catalogs from platforms where users typically begin their information searches. In October 2005, OCLC's technical staff launched a wiki-like project allowing readers and librarians to add commentary and structured-field information to any WorldCat record. Libraries, museums, historical societies, colleges, and universities use OCLC Preservation Services to preserve printed works, books, maps, manuscripts, and newspapers in microfilm format, which has a 500-year life expectancy. Additionally, OCLC Preservation Services converts print and microfilm materials into digital objects for computer access. OCLC maintains a database for cataloging and searching purposes, which is utilized by librarians and the public. The database contains records in Machine-Readable Cataloging (MARC) standards format, contributed by library catalogers worldwide who use OCLC as a cataloging tool. These MARC records are downloaded into libraries' local catalog systems, enabling libraries to find and download records for materials they wish to add to their catalogs without undergoing the lengthy process of individual cataloging. This database remains the world's largest bibliographic database, containing over 1 billion cataloged items. WorldCat is also publicly searchable through a web-based service called FirstSearch and the Open WorldCat program. In 1988, OCLC acquired the trademark and copyrights associated with the Dewey Decimal Classification System by purchasing Forest Press. WebJunction, a division of OCLC, is funded by a grant from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. QuestionPoint is a reference management service provided by OCLC that equips libraries with tools to communicate with users through various channels. This 24/7 reference service is supported by a cooperative network of participating libraries worldwide. Regional service providers contract with OCLC to deliver support and training for OCLC services. These providers ensure that libraries can effectively utilize OCLC's offerings.
